Name: Harriers - Subfamily Circinae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter.
Habitat: Marshes, fields and prairies.
Foods: Rodents, reptiles, amphibians and birds.
Economics: Marsh hawk is the representive in this subfamily.
Name: Ospreys - Family Pandionidae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall.
Habitat: Rivers and lakes. Nests normally in high open places, sometimes on ground.
Foods: Fish.
Miscellaneous: Only hawk that dives into water for fish.
Name: Falcons - Subfamily Falconinae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter.
Habitat: Wide-ranging, nearly cosmopolitan.
Foods: Birds, rodents, insects.
Miscellaneous: Three species dicussed in text.
Name: Hungarian or Gray Partiridge - Perdix perdix
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter.
Habitat: Open farmland, grainfields, Nests in grasslined hollow in grass or brush.
Foods: Wheat (1), barley (1), bromegrass (2), alfalfa (3), clover (3), sunflower (3), and insects.
Miscellaneous: Introduced species. Important game bird.
Name: Sandhill Crane - Grus canadensis
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall.
Habitat: Praries, grainfields, marshes and mountain meadows. Nests in marshes on ground.
Foods: Mostly domestic crops (corn, wheat, oats) and grasses, also insects, small mammals (rodents), amphibians and snails.
Miscellaneous: Hunted in some areas for meat. Relative of the endangered whooping crane.
Name: Rails and Coots - Family Railidae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall.
Habitat: Ponds, lakes, marshes. Rails build grass cup in marsley areas for nesting. Coots nest in seeds or vegetation rafts on ponds and lakes.
Foods: Pondweed, bulrush, algae, duckweed, saltgrass, insects, crustaceans, small fish and mollusks.
Miscellaneous: Coot is second only to the mollard and pintail in population numbers.
Name: Plovers - Family Charadriidae
Montana resident in: Spring, summer, fall, winter, migratory only.
Habitat: Shorelines, grasslands, plains, mudflats and open marshes.
